Reposting top answers from the other thread since starting the same discussion over and over again from a blank slate is counterproductive:

@Undeleted:

Kind of seems like the antithesis of having an open forum. As you stated, you're well aware that anything posted is in the public domain, so you should also realize that everything is historically archived - if not by voat natively, then by any number of third-party archiving sites.

Don't want people to go through your shit? Don't post shit.

@TheAutomaton:

I have only ever needed to go through another users account for doxing/info gathering.

Well, a lot of people aren't interested in doxxing anyone, but going through post history does help to establish credibility.

If someone posts a comment that starts, 'Brain surgeon here', I can look through his post history and if I see that yesterday he started a comment, 'Astronaut here' and the day before that he claimed to be a mother of 6 and a sixteen year old boy within a couple hours of each other, I can come to the conclusion that he's a chronic liar and that his expertise should be totally ignored on any topic he posts about.

Yes, obviously being able to view a person's post history can be used for 'evil', but I think the onus is on the poster to try to be aware and be careful about posting self-identifying information on a website full of total strangers. Being able to browse a person's post history lets you know if you're dealing with a troll, compulsive liar, etc and I think that's too valuable to give up just to try to protect the people who are over-sharing in the first place.

Be careful what you post about yourself online!

@reacher:

Transparency is key to a site like this.

@she:

I think it keeps people honest. Also, if voat didn't do it for you, a bot would do it for someone else.

Also think of users who down the line maybe on voat simply to just market a product, being able to go over someone's comment history provides transparency to the site overall.

@SurvivorType:
